rounds.text: Modern Malleables Ltd is severely under-appreciated by the market, presenting an exceptional margin of safety of 48.4% with intrinsic value estimated at Rs 115 against its current market price of Rs 59.6 [E40, E41]. The reverse DCF model reveals that the current price merely prices in a modest 8.9% earnings growth, vastly underestimating the robust base-case assumption of 18.0% [E42]. This conservative valuation ignores extraordinary fundamental momentum, highlighted by trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 93% and profit growth of 96% [E17, E21]. Furthermore, the company has transformed its balance sheet into a fortress by aggressively slashing borrowings to just Rs 3 Cr in Sep 2026 from Rs 12 Cr a year prior, achieving an almost debt-free status with a negligible debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x [E33, E34, E47]. Operational efficiency is also surging, evidenced by a dramatic jump in quarterly operating margin to 27% in Sep 2026 compared to 15% in the same quarter last year [E27], alongside a structural compression in working capital requirements from 145 days down to 90.7 days [E50]. Conceded: cash conversion stands at a weak 0.37x against reported profit [E30], and the 5-year median return on equity is muted at 8% [E23].

Modern Malleables Ltd carries significant valuation and quality risks that undermine its recent price momentum. The company’s cash conversion stands at a concerning 0.37x for March 2026, revealing that reported profits are running far ahead of actual cash generation, which warrants close scrutiny of receivables and accruals [E30]. This cash disconnect is further reinforced by worsening debtor days, which have increased from 75.0 to 93.1 days [E54]. Furthermore, despite reporting repeated profits, the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4, E52]. Valuation multiples also appear stretched compared to peers, with the stock trading at an EV/EBITDA of 15.36x against a sector benchmark of 12.22x [E11], alongside a price-to-book ratio of 3.24x [E2]. Historical return on equity profiles are weak, highlighted by a median ROE of just 7% over the last 3 years [E24] and a low 3-year average ROE of 6.84% [E53]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months reaches 93% and compounded profit growth hits 96% [E17, E21].

Conceded: cash conversion is 0.37x for March 2026 [E30] and debtor days increased to 93.1 [E54]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4] and the 3-year median ROE is 7% [E24]. However, the bear's focus on historical ROE ignores a surging operational present where quarterly operating margin reached 27% in September 2026 compared to 15% a year prior [E27]. Furthermore, the company's financial risk is heavily mitigated because it is almost debt free with borrowings falling to Rs 3 Cr in September 2026 and a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.01x [E33, E34, E47]. While EV/EBITDA stands at 15.36x [E11], this is supported by exceptional top-line and bottom-line acceleration, including a trailing twelve month sales growth of 93% and profit growth of 96% [E17, E21]. Finally, working capital requirements have actually improved overall, contracting substantially from 145 days down to 90.7 days [E50].

Conceded: borrowings fell to Rs 3 Cr and the debt-to-equity ratio sits at 0.01x [E33, E34]. However, citing a surging operational present does not erase structural profitability flaws, evidenced by a low 3-year median ROE of just 7% [E24] and an inconsistent yearly operating margin trend [E28]. While TTM sales and profit growth reached 93% and 96% [E17, E21], the screen explicitly flags that earnings growth is now decelerating [E60]. Furthermore, price growth has catastrophically outpaced profit growth by 1216%, proving that expectations are running dangerously ahead of delivery [E44]. Conceded: working capital requirements contracted to 90.7 days [E50], but debtor days simultaneously worsened from 75.0 to 93.1 days [E54], directly corroborating poor cash conversion of 0.37x where profits far exceed actual cash [E30]. Finally, pointing to an EV/EBITDA of 15.36x misses that it trades at a premium to the sector benchmark of 12.22x [E11], supported by zero dividend yield [E4] despite repeated reporting of profits [E52].
